candidates.claim: A public request might reach a mutable backend action without the stronger route-specific authorization check.
candidates.independent_verifier: server/route inventory and route-local authorization contract
candidates.reason: The public edge exposes read-only API methods; the mutable hunter action has an additional configured strong-auth gate.

candidates.claim: Advisory capability metadata might become execution authority.
candidates.independent_verifier: call-site enumeration for RadarEngine.scanFixtures and DecisionKernel consumer review
candidates.reason: The current canonical caller is fixture-only and the decision kernel has no execution sink.

candidates.claim: A HumanGate approval might apply to a different proposed action.
candidates.reason: Gate and resume identities change when proposed_action changes; resolving one gate does not resolve the other.

candidates.claim: Browser execution might escape the configured origin boundary.
candidates.reason: Initial target, HTTP subrequests and WebSocket connections are constrained to the allowed-origin set.

candidates.claim: Sensitive browser observations might persist unredacted in evidence.
candidates.reason: Persistent and broadcast event sinks receive normalized redacted fields/payloads.

candidates.claim: Public responses might lack a common browser security policy.
candidates.reason: The candidate applies a common policy to public HTML/assets/JSON and preserves stricter private CSP.

candidates.claim: Private routes might be reachable through path normalization variants.
candidates.reason: Normalization and concealment happen before public asset/API routing and excessive encoding fails closed.

candidates.claim: Release evidence might accept ancestry instead of exact tag/main equality.
candidates.reason: v1.5.0 requires explicit dispatch and exact remote main/tag equality; ancestry checks are forbidden.

hardening_only: The general compatibility authorization fallback should not be used as the sole guard for future mutable routes.
Unused in-page auth-preview instrumentation should be removed or redesigned before any future bridge consumes it.
The GitLab mirror workflow should eventually pin checkout to a commit SHA.
Wrangler is invoked at an exact version; exact Worker-version identity remains the release artifact-integrity control.
